name: Days to Maturity Calculator
seoTitle: Days to Maturity Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Days to maturity tells you whether a crop will finish before the season does. Free days to maturity calculator: enter your values and get harvest day of year,
summary:
Days to maturity tells you whether a crop will finish before the season does. It returns harvest day of year, harvest month, days implied by the GDD target and days remaining after harvest (season 220 days), and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator converts a variety's maturity rating into a calendar date, adjusting for sowing date and the heat the season is actually delivering. The arithmetic keeps full precision internally and only rounds what it displays, so the number you copy out is the number the formula produced. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Days to Maturity
sections.html:
Harvest day = sowing day + days to maturity

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
sowing dayday of year the crop was sownday
DTMdays to maturity for the varietydays
GDDheat required, an alternative to DTM°C·day

sections.title: How do I use the Days to Maturity?
sections.html:
Fill the boxes you have numbers for; the calculator decides what it can derive from them.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: sowing day of year of 120 day, days to maturity of 95 days, gdd to maturity of 1,400 GDD, average gdd per day of 13 GDD/day.

Substituting them into the formula gives harvest day of year of 215 day, harvest month of 8, days implied by the gdd target of 107.69 days, days remaining after harvest (season 220 days) of 5 days.

Because the example uses the defaults, you can reproduce it by loading the page and reading the results panel before touching anything.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Catalogue days-to-maturity ratings assume a reference temperature; a cool season stretches them and a hot one shortens them, which is why GDD is the better input.

  • Divide the GDD target by the average daily accumulation to get days — a crop needing 1 400 GDD at 13 GDD/day takes about 108 days.

  • Late sowing in a shortening season often needs a shorter-maturity variety rather than more inputs.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
Before blaming the formula, check these — they explain nearly every mismatch:

  • Counting from emergence in one place and from sowing in another.
  • Using last year's GDD accumulation for this year's forecast.
  • Assuming a fixed harvest date ignores the difference between physiological and harvest maturity.

faq.q: What does days to maturity mean?
faq.a: The number of days from sowing (or transplanting) to a marketable or physiologically mature crop.

faq.q: Why does my crop mature later than the packet says?
faq.a: Cooler than expected weather; the rating assumes a reference temperature.

faq.q: What does the Days to Maturity actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns harvest day of year, harvest month, days implied by the GDD target and days remaining after harvest (season 220 days). Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
